name: Emeka Petrov

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I am from the Work Futures Panel, an independent research group with no ties to employers, AI companies, unions, parties or government. Your answers are confidential. What does an ordinary day at the accounting firm look like?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: The sports hall's membership fees arrive in batches, and I check the cancelled memberships before entering the accounts and preparing its tax schedule for review. I like finding why a member was charged twice; I dislike the rush to close a file when the club has not sent its refund list. I am 58, with a bachelor's degree in accounting, and I am a junior still learning these returns. I use AI now and then to sort a first list of missing items, but I check it against the bank and ask my supervisor about doubtful entries.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau. Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: If AI remains a small helper, the hall still needs someone to match fees and refunds. The sorting list can save me a little time without deciding the tax figure.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the team a cancelled membership needs a bank check before the return is signed. I would tell the hall manager which refunds are still missing.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: My pay is around the usual rate for an accountant and my partner Maren and I have five months of expenses set aside. Our grown children live on their own, the household bills are covered while we both work, and some accounting firms are nearby; I still want to know what retirement could actually pay.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would keep preparing the paid hall accounts and checking the occasional approved AI list against the bank. I would ask my supervisor Leah for the hall's complete refund schedule before I close the return, and keep the five-month reserve available if a real income gap comes.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel uneasy about the later years, but the current work and five months of cash feel steady. The hall's missing refund list bothers me more than modest AI.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you change firms for a little more pay?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Not for a little. Some nearby firms exist, but I would want a written offer that keeps our regular bills covered before moving.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you tell the children?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell our grown children we have saved for an interruption, not that they must provide one. They have their own households to run.

say: I would require a **bank check** for cancelled memberships.
I would ask for the **refund schedule** before closing a return.
think: Our **five-month reserve** and current wages keep near-term bills manageable.
I still need actual **retirement figures** before planning a date.
do: Keep **paid hall accounts** and verify approved AI lists against the bank.
Request the **complete refund schedule** before filing the hall return.
feel: I feel **uneasy** about later income, though current work feels steady.
S0.quote: The hall's missing refund list bothers me more than modest AI.
fieldNote: His occasional AI list remains a **sorting aid**, with the bank and supervisor governing the return.
The five-month reserve is **already saved** and held for a genuine gap; he is not claiming a new deposit.

steps.text: Keep paid hall accounts and check approved AI lists and refunds against bank
Request complete membership-refund schedule before closing the hall return

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption. Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The fee matching and return drafting are thinking work the new systems could take. Robots reach physical hall cleaning later; my desk would be affected first.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask the firm to show junior staff the errors before it shortens a rota. I would say a member wrongly charged twice still needs a person to put it right.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: My own junior hours could shrink if one reviewer checks more of these files. Five months saved would buy a search, but Maren's school-office wage alone would not cover our regular bills for long.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask Leah for a two-week paid comparison of anonymised hall accounts against signed originals, only with written manager approval. If it passes, I would learn the approved checker on paid time and use it live only after written sign-off; if it fails or is refused, I would keep the authorised paid checks while offered. If my hours fall in the first year, I would take a posted accounts-clerk job only with written pay, hours and start date covering our bills and the journey.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about possible loss of my own shifts. A careful test is useful, but it cannot promise the same hours afterward.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What errors would you look for?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would count cancelled memberships still treated as income and refunds left out. Leah would sign the comparison with me before any live change.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you commute farther?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Only if the written wage after travel still covers our bills. Some firms are nearby, so I would check a real local opening before taking an expensive journey.

say: I would request **error evidence** before rota cuts.
I would keep a **person accountable** for wrongly charged members.
think: My own **junior hours** could fall as matching speeds up.
Maren's wage would not replace my **typical accounting pay** for long.
do: Test **two weeks** of anonymised hall accounts against signed originals on paid time with written approval; otherwise keep paid checks.
Learn the **approved checker** after a signed pass on paid time; use live only with written sign-off.
After cuts take a **posted clerk role** only with written after-travel bill-covering pay, hours and start.
feel: I feel **anxious** about fewer paid shifts.
S1.quote: A careful test is useful, but it cannot promise the same hours afterward.
fieldNote: He is willing to learn after a **signed paid trial**; the failed or refused test leaves authorised paid checks in place.
Travel cost is a **wage gate**, not a reason to treat every nearby firm as a guaranteed opening.

steps.text: Test accounts against signed originals for two paid weeks with written approval; otherwise keep paid checks
Learn checker on paid time after signed pass; use live only with written sign-off
After cuts take posted clerk job with written after-travel bill-covering pay hours start

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028. Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: AGI in 2028 could match the fees, question a refund and draft the tax schedule at my desk. Robots around 2031 might later clean the hall, but they do not postpone the accounts change.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask the partners to give junior staff notice and exact last-paid-shift dates. I would tell the hall manager to keep a named contact for disputed fees.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I expect most of my junior accounting hours to go when AGI handles the memberships. Five months saved gives Maren and me time to search, but losing my wage would still force us to cut household spending; I lie awake thinking about the fifth month.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Now I would delay our planned rail holiday and move its monthly budget into emergency cash while my pay continues. I would keep paid hall files while assigned; if the job ends in the first year after 2028, I would use the reserve for bills and apply to posted sports-centre admissions jobs, taking one only with written pay, hours and a start date that cover our basic bills after travel. Admissions also uses booking screens, so I would count an actual paid offer as a bridge, not a refuge.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel alarmed because I expect a large loss of paid hours. A five-month reserve is valuable, but it is not a new job.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you accept a job that needs evening shifts?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Only if Maren and I agree on the actual hours and the written wage after travel covers bills. We do not have child pickup now, but we still need our shared transport to work.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if no admissions job is posted?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would keep the paid firm work still offered and use the reserve only after a gap opens. An advert that does not exist cannot be put into our budget.

say: I would seek **last-paid-shift dates** for juniors before the firm changes the hall accounts rota.
I would keep a **named fee contact** for members.
think: I expect a **large loss** of my accounting hours after 2028.
Five months saved buys time, but not a **replacement wage**.
do: Delay the **rail holiday** and deposit its monthly budget while pay continues.
Keep **paid hall files** while assigned; after job loss use reserve for bills.
Take a **posted admissions role** only with written after-travel bill-covering pay, hours, start and agreed evening rota.
feel: I feel **alarmed** by expected loss of paid hours.
S2.quote: A five-month reserve is valuable, but it is not a new job.
fieldNote: His 2028 **screen-work exposure** precedes the later physical hall robots, and admissions booking remains exposed.
He makes **new cash deposits** from a postponed holiday only while paid; the existing reserve funds a real gap.

steps.text: Delay rail holiday and deposit monthly budget while paid work continues
Keep paid hall files while assigned; after loss use reserve for bills
Take posted admissions job with written after-travel bill-covering pay hours start and agreed rota

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031. Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Five years gives me time to try a different office task while the paid hall returns still arrive. AGI reaches those desk accounts in 2031; robots around 2034 are later for physical hall work.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask the hall to post a paid membership-appeals clerk place if it actually needs one. I would not buy a course because someone said customer contact is the future.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The tax-entry fee may fall, but I already know which refund cases upset members. I am still a junior learner, so any appeals work would need a supervisor and a real wage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would handle one membership appeal each month only if Leah assigns it with paid supervision. I would use the hall's free policy notes while keeping paid returns; if a posted appeals-clerk place comes with funded training fees, paid study hours and written pay, hours and start date covering bills after travel, I would take it. In the first year after 2031, if my accounting hours end before such a place exists, I would use the reserve for bills during the search.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about the tax work thinning, but five years lets me test whether a paid appeals place exists. A member's thank-you note is not a wage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if Leah cannot assign an appeal?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Then I would keep the paid accounts files still offered and read the free notes. I would not answer a member alone without training and authority.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you take a distant role?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Only if the written wage after travel covers our basic bills and the hours fit Maren's actual school-office rota. A posted role is a start, not an offer I can accept blind.

I would reject an **unfunded course** offered as a job plan.
think: My member-refund knowledge needs **paid supervision** before it becomes another role.

Read **free policy notes**; take a posted appeals place only with funded fees and paid study hours.
Take the **posted appeals job** only with written after-travel bill-covering pay, hours, start and agreed rota.

S3.quote: A member's thank-you note is not a wage.
fieldNote: His appeals plan depends on a **posted paid place**, supervised casework and training costs covered by the employer.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036. Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Ten years brings me to 68 before AGI reaches the accounts desk in 2036. Robots around 2039 are later for hall cleaning, and I cannot assume my junior accounts hours last that long.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask the firm for a year-by-year paid-hours plan, and the retirement provider for actual income figures. I would tell Maren the two documents have to be read together.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would like fewer hours someday, but I do not know what income would replace them. Five months saved helps with a short break, not an open-ended stop from work.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would request a written retirement-income statement and a written reduced-hours offer, then compare their combined income with our basic bills before changing my schedule. I would keep assigned paid hall returns while they exist; in the first year after 2036, if the job ends and the figures do not cover bills, I would use the reserve for bills and seek a posted clerk role only with written pay, hours and start date covering basic costs after travel. I would reduce paid hours only if the written combined income actually meets those costs.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel uneasy about the distant loss of a familiar desk, but I can check real numbers over ten years. I would rather work fewer honest hours than retire on a guess.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if the retirement statement is smaller than you hoped?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Then I would keep the paid work available and search actual posted openings if it ends. I will not set a date using five months of cash as if it were lifetime income.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would Maren also cut her hours?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Only after my partner Maren checks her own school-office schedule and income. We cannot both step back on two untested estimates.

say: I would ask for **paid-hours and income figures** before reducing work.
I would read **both household schedules** before making a date.
think: I do not know what retirement income would **replace my wage**.
Five months saved cannot fund an **open-ended stop** from work.
do: Request **written retirement figures** and a reduced-hours offer; cut hours only if combined income covers bills.
Keep **paid hall returns** while offered; after loss use reserve for bills if income falls short.
Seek **posted clerk work** after 2036 loss only if income falls short, with written after-travel bill-covering pay, hours and start.
feel: I feel **uneasy** about a distant desk loss, with time to check figures.
S4.quote: I would rather work fewer honest hours than retire on a guess.
fieldNote: At 68 he explores a **conditional reduction in hours**, without assuming any pension amount or entitlement.
His written **combined-income test** governs the choice; paid work remains available only while offered and any new role needs posted terms.

steps.text: Request written retirement figures and reduced-hours offer; cut hours only if combined income covers bills
Keep paid hall returns while offered; after loss use reserve if income falls short
Seek posted clerk work after 2036 loss if income insufficient; require written after-travel bill-covering pay/start/hours

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most because I could lose the work that pays our regular bills long before I know whether retirement income could replace it. A paid, posted role with written hours and wages would help, as would notice of the last paid shift.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn't ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: You did not ask whether a cancelled membership makes me feel foolish when I miss it. I still check the bank line twice because I want the member's refund to be real.

headlineQuote: I still check the bank line twice because I want the member's refund to be real.
portrait: Emeka is a **58-year-old junior accountant** with a bachelor's degree who is still learning hall returns.
His **typical pay**, five-month reserve and some nearby firms give limited but real search room.
He uses AI **occasionally** and wants signed, paid testing before a new checker reaches live accounts.
He explores a **paid membership-appeals place** and later reduced hours only against written household income.
biggestWorry: The **2028 AGI** case may remove his junior hours before another paid role exists.
whatWouldHelp: He wants **last-paid-shift notice** and a posted role with written wages and hours covering bills.
